Ben / Vivek —

Draft answers below; feel free to edit for tone before we send. I'm attaching the runbook excerpt and replication diagram.

1) RTO / RPO (hosted API — Redwood Managed):
- RTO (regional outage resulting in traffic shift): automated routing adjustment completed within 30–45 seconds for control-plane routing (DNS and edge-level reroute). Application-level warm-up (model KV cache + prefix cache) depends on traffic profile — typical priming to reach 90% of steady-state latency observed in load tests is 2–6 minutes for conversational workloads; for short-sequence generation (<=128 tokens) median priming time is ~90–120 seconds.
- RPO: customer-facing persistent records (billing events, audit logs) are written to durable object storage with multi-AZ replication and cross-region asynchronous replication. Typical observed cross-region replication lag is under 60 seconds for metadata and under 5 minutes for large batched logs. For Dedicated and Private deployments we offer synchronous replication options (per contract) delivering sub-60s RPO for critical artifacts.

2) Routing / model-fallback sequence for multi-region events:
- Hosted (default): active-active edge routing with policy-based smart routing. On detection of regional failure we perform an automated route shift to healthy regions at the edge; fallback to a lower-capacity model variant is available if GPU capacity is constrained. Sequence: detect -> withdraw region from pool -> edge DNS + peer routing update -> traffic flows to secondary -> model cache miss rate spikes -> cache rehydration. Typical time to first response served in secondary ~ <10s; median steady-state latency recovered when cache primed (see RTO above).
- Dedicated: routing is customer-configurable. We document an automated and a manual cutover path; manual cutovers require runbook steps around load balancer and VPC peering and typically take 10–40 minutes depending on network propagation.

3) Cache priming and transient errors:
- KV/prefix cache is in-memory per-GPU process. On regional cutover, we expect a short window of increased 429/503 at the application tail for cold hot paths. In our failover simulations for similar customers, peak transient error rate at cutover was <2% and decayed to baseline within the priming window above. We provide optional warm-warm replication (stateful session mirroring) for customers with strict SLAs.

4) Data durability and replication for logs, audit trails, billing:
- Audit/billing events: written synchronously to a durable write-ahead log in primary region and asynchronously replicated to a cross-region object store. Retention and replication policy configurable per-customer.
- Backups: nightly snapshots of critical metadata; critical metadata snapshots retained for 90 days by default; longer retention available.

5) Manual runbook actions and estimated operator time:
- Hosted automated path: zero operator steps in normal scenarios — cutover is automatic. If operator intervention required (manual failback, legal hold), typical playbook steps: confirm region health, trigger rollback routing, validate parity, confirm data replication completion. Estimated operator time: 10–25 minutes for most rollback scenarios.

Evidence attached: redwood-runbook-cutover-v1.3.pdf (cutover checklist excerpt), s3-replication-diagram.png, SOC2_Type2_summary.pdf (redacted). Also linking our internal rehearsal log (redacted) in the response.

Notes / caveats to surface to Anthem: exact priming times are workload-dependent (model size, request shape, and prefix reuse). For large-batch embedding workloads warm-up patterns differ; call this out in the response.

-monica

Lena / Chris —

Thanks for the appendix. Please find Redwood's responses and supporting evidence attached. Highlights: 

- Hosted API: automated active-active routing with edge-based failover; routing cut completes within ~30–45s. Application-level priming to reach steady-state typically completes in 2–6 minutes depending on workload; short-sequence workloads recover faster (~1–2 minutes).
- RPO: durable records replicate cross-region with observed metadata lag <60s and batched logs <5 minutes. Synchronous replication options available on Dedicated / Private.
- Transient errors: short spike in transient 429/503 is expected during cache rehydration; our simulations showed peak transient error <2% and recovery to baseline within priming window. Optional warm-warm session mirroring is available for stricter SLAs.
- Manual steps: Hosted automated cutover requires no operator steps for most scenarios; rollback or manual migration documented in the attached runbook. Estimated operator intervention when required: 10–25 minutes.

Attachments included: redwood-runbook-cutover-v1.3.pdf; s3-replication-diagram.png; SOC2_Type2_summary.pdf.

Next steps — would you like a short technical walkthrough of the attachments and a live cutover demo? We can schedule a 60-minute session and run a controlled failover rehearsal on a synthetic tenant. Proposed slots: Dec 8 or Dec 10 morning PST.

Thanks — looking forward to your feedback.

Ben Carter

Ben —

Thanks for the quick turnaround and the attachments. A couple clarifications before we present to our resiliency committee: 

1) You mention 'active-active edge routing' — can you confirm whether model-state replication is active-active or active-passive? In particular we need to know whether in a regional outage requests hitting the secondary region will see session continuity (same KV state) or if sessions will be rehydrated from persisted storage.

2) For the optional 'warm-warm session mirroring' you reference pricing/availability — can you provide the standard SLA language you propose for that option and any historical rehearsal logs (redacted) showing recovery timelines?

Attached: Anthem_DR_Scenario_matrix.xlsx

If we can get those clarifications and an available slot for the Dec 14th rehearsal, we can move this into the vendor evaluation package.

Regards,
Lena Ortiz
Senior Procurement Manager — Anthem Health
